title: FIRST &
opening_copy: The line is not on the grass. The truck draws it into the picture every frame, from what the camera sensors report.
closing_kicker: MIC LINE · SURVEY · LENS · REGISTRATION · COLOURS · RENDER · KEYER · AIR
closing_copy: Every frame, on every play, from the same few assumptions: the field is surveyed, the cameras are registered, and nothing has moved since.

title: CABLE TO
EVERY POSITION
chapters.copy: The trucks park in the compound. Fiber runs to each instrumented camera deck, and every camera sends its picture and its sensor data home on that one cable.

title: EVERY MOVE
IS MEASURED
chapters.copy: Pan and tilt are counted inside the head; the digital lens reports zoom, focus and the 2X extender. An ebox on the side of the camera turns those numbers into audio on the camera’s MIC 2 input. The operator frames the shot; the sensors report every move.

title: THE SENSOR DATA
RIDES THE AUDIO
chapters.copy: The ebox turns the encoder readings into tones on the camera’s MIC 2 input. They ride the fiber with the picture, leave the CCU as MIC 2 audio, and a decoder turns them back into numbers for the tracking computer. Early lenses had encoders bolted on; a 2010s digital lens reports zoom, focus and the extender itself.

title: THE FIELD ISN’T FLAT
chapters.copy: Fields are crowned so rain runs off, often about a foot higher down the middle. The crew surveys it and fits a curve across each measured yard line. The line is drawn on that surface, not on a flat plane.

title: TEACH IT THE
LENS FIRST
chapters.copy: The lens first. Lock on an object at full zoom, zoom all the way out and mark it in three images: the drift of the mark is the image centre. A known pan that puts it on the frame edge gives the focal length in pixels. Straight edges, marked in every image, give the distortion. Then again with the 2X in.

title: TEACH IT
THE COLOURS
chapters.copy: Before kickoff the operator samples the grass the line may cover and every colour on both uniforms it must never cover. The light will not stay put: sun to shade, the banks coming on, snow. Whenever it changes, the grass is sampled again, during the game.

title: COUNTS IN,
PIXELS OUT
chapters.copy: Each frame, the counts become angles and a focal length. Every point of the line, sitting on the surveyed crown, is projected through that camera model into the picture.

title: THE LINE GOES UNDER
chapters.copy: Every pixel under the line is split into brightness and two colour-difference channels and compared with the trained colours. Grass lets the line through. Jerseys, pants and helmets stop it.

title: FRAME-ACCURATE
OR NOTHING
chapters.copy: Program video is held back a few frames while the graphic renders. Time code pairs every frame with the sensor packet from the same instant, and tally tells the system which camera is on air.

title: NOTHING IS
ALLOWED TO MOVE
chapters.copy: The model assumes the rig, the lens and the lighting stay exactly as they were at training. Re-balance a head, bump a tripod or swap a lens, and the line is wrong until that camera is registered again.

title: WHEN THE PAINT
DISAPPEARS
chapters.copy: Under heavy snow the same system can draw the whole field: yard lines, sidelines and the line to gain. The keyer is retrained so the lines draw on the snow.
